title: Arborly POC: Proof-of-Impact Brief and Success Criteria
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the objectives, scope, workshop plan, and measurable success criteria for the Arborly POC (2-week sprint). Arborly (retail supply optimisation) is trying to validate that Redwood Inference can reduce cognitive time-to-action for store managers by producing accurate, high-confidence restock recommendations from transaction + inventory streams. The goal of this engagement is to demonstrate a customer-impact signal (reduction in manual lookups and faster reorder decisions) and to produce a deployable inference pipeline design that Arborly's platform team can move into pilot.

High-level goals (what success looks like for Arborly and Redwood):
- Customer impact (primary): 20% reduction in average time store managers spend on daily restock lookups for pilot SKUs (measured by timestamped UI events + surveys).
- Accuracy and trust (primary): Precision@Top1 >= 85% for recommended restock action on the evaluation holdout set representative of live traffic. Confidence calibration: predicted confidence correlates with correctness (Brier score <= 0.18).
- Latency and SLOs (secondary): 95th percentile end-to-end suggestion latency <= 350ms for hosted API path; fallbacks to lightweight heuristics < 150ms if model unavailable.
- Cost and economics (secondary): Cost per 1k recommendations under Redwood Dedicated or Hosted <= customer target (baseline target $2.50 per 1k).
- Deployability (operational): Produce a deployment design (hosted + on-prem-compatible variant) with clear data ingress, key rotation plan, and an A/B rollout checklist.

Scope of the POC (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope:
  - Three-week technical engagement broken into a 1-week setup + 1-week evaluation + 1-week workshop and wrap-up (we will compress or extend to two weeks if both parties agree).
  - Ingest of anonymised daily transactions and inventory snapshots for 5 pilot stores and ~200 SKUs (customer-provided extract).
  - Implement a Redwood inference route that returns the top-3 restock actions and confidence scores per SKU; support for streaming and batched calls for backfill evaluation.
  - Synthetic user-facing UI hooks to capture time-to-action in a controlled pilot environment (instrumentation spec provided).
- Out-of-scope:
  - Full integration with Arborly production systems, payment or billing, and long-term data retention beyond the POC window.
  - Training a brand-new model from scratch; POC will evaluate a curated open model family + lightweight finetune/adapter if needed.

Acceptance tests and detailed success criteria:
- Functional tests:
  - Endpoint returns valid JSON with fields: sku, recommended_action, confidence, explanation_snippet within 200ms median for single-shot requests during baseline test.
  - Batch evaluation job completes on the supplied holdout set within agreed compute budget (T-shirt size: <4 GPU-hours).
- Accuracy tests:
  - Precision@Top1 >= 85% and Recall@3 >= 92% on holdout; if below thresholds, a documented action plan with tuning steps must be delivered.
  - Confidence calibration measured via reliability diagram and Brier score <= 0.18.
- UX/impact tests:
  - Instrumented pilot shows median time-to-action drop >= 15% across pilot managers and at least one store hits >=20% improvement.
  - At least 6 out of 8 targeted pilot users rate suggestions as "useful" or "very useful" in a short post-task survey.
- Operational tests:
  - Failover: Simulated model-instance outage triggers automatic fallback heuristic and system continues to respond within latency SLOs for 95% of calls.
  - Cost projection: Completed cost-per-1k estimate with sensitivity analysis (batch sizes, KV cache hit rates).

Workshop plan and agenda (week 2):
- Day 1: Data walkthrough, schema alignment, and privacy checklist (2 hours). Deliverable: data mapping doc and anonymisation confirmation.
- Day 2: Model/behavior review, decision log on model family selection (3 hours). Deliverable: selected model and param table.
- Day 3: Integration patterns & rollout strategy (2 hours). Deliverable: lightweight deployment blueprint (hosted + private fallback).
- Day 4: Metrics, observability, and acceptance tests walkthrough (90 minutes). Deliverable: instrumentation spec, eval notebook.
- Day 5: Executive demo and next-steps alignment (60 minutes). Deliverable: final slide deck and prioritized handoff checklist.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood (SE lead: Priya Menon): overall POC delivery, API implementation, metrics instrumentation, and ops blueprint.
- Redwood (ML engineer: Ethan Cho): model selection, calibration checks, batch evaluation job.
- Redwood (SRE liaison: Ravi Singh): deployment pattern draft and fallback runbooks.
- Arborly (Product owner: Claire Mercer): data provision, pilot coordinator, and acceptance sign-off.
- Arborly (Engineering: Marcos Reyes): ingestion endpoints and dev/test environment access.

Data handling & security notes:
- Data provided to Redwood must be anonymised at source: PII removed, store IDs hashed, SKU identifiers consistent but not reversible. We will sign an updated DPA/TOU addendum if the customer requires an on-prem agent.
- Key material: For private pilot mode we will test KMS integration with Arborly test keys; production KMS keys are out-of-scope.
- Logging: No raw transaction logs will leave Arborly’s environment in the private deployment path; in hosted evaluation, only aggregated evaluation metrics and minimal examples (with consent) will be shared.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Data mismatch between sandbox extract and live traffic leading to overoptimistic accuracy. Mitigation: run a short tail test with a random sample of live events and flag distribution drift in the initial workshop.
- Risk: Model produces plausible but incorrect actions (hallucinations). Mitigation: apply conservative confidence thresholding and require human-in-loop confirmation for actions above threshold during pilot.
- Risk: Latency spikes under peak. Mitigation: configure autoscaling policy + route critical UI calls to a smaller quantized variant.

Deliverables (end of POC):
- Evaluation report with metrics (accuracy, calibration, latency distribution, cost estimates).
- Lightweight deployment blueprint and rollback checklist (hosted path + private variant).
- Instrumentation spec and minimal demo UI for time-to-action measurement.
- Handoff package: README, runbook, sample eval notebook, Jira tickets for production rollout.

Metrics dashboard proposal (minimally required):
- Precision@1, Recall@3, Brier score, 50/95/99 latency percentiles, cache hit rate, tokens-per-recommendation, cost-per-1k, pilot user satisfaction rating.

Immediate next steps (week 0 prework):
1) Arborly to provide anonymised sample extract (5 pilot stores, 14 days) + schema by 2025-01-20.
2) Redwood to provision temporary hosted sandbox API + seed model and share endpoint by 2025-01-22.
3) Joint workshop scheduling (choose two 2-hour blocks) by 2025-01-21.
4) Sign off on data DPA and access list by 2025-01-23.

Notes / open questions (to resolve in Day 1 workshop):
- Can Arborly share a lightweight store manager instrumentation stub or do we need to deliver the stub?
- Is there an internal SLA for suggestions being editable by managers (audit requirement)?
- Confirmation on cost target (hosted vs dedicated) and acceptable compute envelope for the POC.

Appendix: Quick evaluation checklist (what we will run during POC)
- Baseline run: run selected model on holdout set, capture Precision@1, Recall@3, Brier score.
- Latency run: 10k synthetic sequential single-shot calls and a 1k parallel burst to capture P50/P95/P99.
- Failover test: kill primary model endpoint for 5 minutes and confirm fallback behavior.
- UX micro-survey: 8 pilot users perform 6 tasks, collect time-to-action and satisfaction rating.
